title: Instrumentation ontology and snapshot for Console analytics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define a clear, versioned instrumentation ontology for Console analytics services and produce a deployable snapshot (metrics, traces, logging envelopes, and dashboard templates) that standardizes how SLIs/SLOs are derived across tenant-aware pipelines. This ticket covers schema design, span/metric naming conventions, trace->metric linking via deterministic IDs, cost-aware sampling policy, and a rollout plan for both streaming ingest and batch reprocessing lanes.
notes: 2025-02-18 - Kickoff: scoped to Console backend services + analytics ingestion (not product-usage UI). Aligning with ENG-4219 observability baseline; decision to keep separate namespace for tenant-scoped SLIs.

2025-02-21 - Draft ontology uploaded to Confluence (see links). Initial review: Design requested concrete examples for prefix/KV cache telemetry and a minimal set of per-tenant SLIs (ingest-latency, enrich-error-rate, downstream-sink-drop-rate).

2025-02-26 - Trade-off discussion: High-cardinality tags vs. pre-aggregation. Agreed to restrict downstream high-cardinality labels to 'tenant_id' and 'route_id' and to use hashed sharding for trace sampling to keep cost bounded.
2025-02-28 - Implemented PoC in analytics ingest transformer (feature branch). End-to-end local test shows correct trace id propagation and metric emission for synthetic probe (see linked PRs).
2025-03-02 - Review feedback from PM (Janelle Ortiz): add acceptance criteria for dashboard templates and a migration sanity check for historical SLI backfills.
2025-03-04 - QA plan drafted: synthetic probes + canary re-ingest of 7 days of compressed events into staging to validate SLI parity within 2% of existing baseline.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned ontology doc (v1) published in Confluence with examples for 10+ common events and metrics.
Console ingest emits metrics and spans conforming to the ontology in staging for synthetic probes.
Tracing linkability: for any emitted metric we can find a representative span via deterministic trace_id propagation for 95% of probe events.
Dashboard templates (Grafana) created for per-tenant SLI view and default alert thresholds wired to staging alerts.
Cost model: sampling policy tested and demonstrates <15% increase in observability cost compared to baseline while improving trace coverage for tail errors.
risks: High-cardinality labels could blow ingestion costs if misapplied by downstream teams.
Backfilling historical SLIs may produce drift vs. current SLOs if transformation logic changes during rollout.
Deterministic sampling hash collision edge cases could bias tenant-level SLI estimates for very small tenants.
decisions: Use 'console.' prefix for all metrics and 'console.span' for trace spans to avoid cross-product naming collisions.
Keep tenant_id as the only high-cardinality dimension carried into long-term metrics; other labels should be aggregated at ingest.
Adopt a two-tier sampling policy: 1/100 default sampling for debug traces, deterministic 100% sampling for synthetic probes and error spans above 5xx rate thresholds.
open_questions: Should we include user_id in short-term logs for debugging despite being sensitive (requires KMS masking)?
What is the acceptable latency budget for observability writes before they are considered impacting production SLOs?
Do Platform teams want the ontology to include explicit quantization buckets for token latency metrics, or leave bucketization to dashboards?
observability_concepts: Trace tagging: service=console-ingest, stage=transform, route_id, tenant_hash
Metric envelopes: name, unit, sample_rate, dataset_version
Logging envelope: structured JSON with event_type, trace_id, span_id, tenant_id (hashed), payload_schema_version
